title: Treaty of Muwatalli II and Alaksandu of Wilusa
summary: Around 1280 BCE the Hittite king Muwatalli II made a treaty with Alaksandu, ruler of Wilusa in western Anatolia, binding him as a vassal. The text survives in the Hittite archives at Hattusa; Wilusa is widely, though not unanimously, identified with Troy (Ilion).

uncertainty.note: About 1280 BCE per two sources; Muwatalli II’s reign is dated 1295-1272 BCE in one chronology and 1315-1297 BCE in another.

where.modern_name: Hattusa (Bogazkale), Corum, Turkey (where the text was found)
where.historical_name: Hattusa, capital of Hatti; Wilusa lay in western Anatolia

importance.justification: A surviving Hittite vassal treaty with Wilusa, a state commonly identified with Troy.
